original_value: Remote sensing by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is significantly important in emergency rescue applications and operations. Particularly, the on‐site images from UAVs can provide valuable information for hazard identification and disaster assessment. In this study, the authors propose a novel method by using back propagation neural networks with feature fusion to detect landslides from UAV images. Specifically, the authors first construct a fundamental shape model of landslides and devise a scale‐invariant feature transform algorithm for feature matching and transformation. By fusing the spatial shape features and spectral features of the landslide, the suspected landslide object from UAV images can be detected initially. Next, the change features of a pre/post‐landslide object are extracted by using the satellite sensing images (before landslide) and the UAV image (after landslide). The authors further feed the change features into the proposed model to enhance the precision and accuracy of landslide detection. They conduct numerous experimental studies with aerospace remote sensing data in two real‐world landslide scenarios. The evaluation results show that the proposed method outperforms baseline algorithms by achieving over 91% accuracy in landslide detection.

result.paraphrase: Remote sensing using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) plays a highly important role in emergency rescue applications and operations. In particular, on-site UAV images can supply valuable information for hazard identification and disaster assessment. In this study, the authors present a new approach that combines back propagation neural networks with feature fusion to detect landslides in UAV imagery. They first build a basic landslide shape model and develop a scale-invariant feature transform algorithm for feature matching and transformation. By merging the landslide’s spatial shape features and spectral features, suspected landslide objects in UAV images can be identified initially. Then, change features for a pre/post-landslide object are extracted using satellite sensing images taken before the landslide and the UAV image captured afterward. These change features are further input into the proposed model to improve landslide detection precision and accuracy. Extensive experiments are carried out with aerospace remote sensing data in two real-world landslide cases. The results indicate that the proposed method surpasses baseline algorithms and achieves more than 91% accuracy in landslide detection.
